key_insight: The paper shows that quantum circuit expressibility is only meaningful when supported by enough samples, leading to an Occam-style law that ties learnable circuit complexity to data availability.
engineering_relevance: For quantum ML practitioners, this provides a principled way to choose ansatz size adaptively from finite data instead of overbuilding circuits that cannot be statistically justified.
method: Define best G-gate approximation error d_G(\hat\rho) and approximate circuit complexity C_\eta(\hat\rho).
Prove an agnostic quantum Occam theorem with excess error scaling like \~O(\sqrt{G/M}).
Derive a model-selection rule and matching lower bounds showing supported complexity scales as G_supported \simeq M\epsilon^2 up to log factors and tomography saturation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical results only: metric-entropy upper bounds, an oracle inequality for adaptive model selection, and matching lower bounds that justify the sample-supported scaling.
watch_item: The law is asymptotic and limited by tomography saturation at 2^n, so very large systems or high-precision regimes may require far more samples than the circuit scaling alone suggests.
paper_title: Quantum Occam Learning: Sample-Supported Expressibility for Circuit-Based Quantum Learning
